A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GM/TGM research and contain 29 readable pages, including Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that all differences are confined to the first-page author line and arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original sequence-generation experiments in Section 6, including biological-design results in Table 2. Appendix B adds experimental parameter sweeps and measured training speeds.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original experiments in Section 6 and Appendix B, including mode rewards, mode-discovery results and training throughput.

M1.justification: The GM regularizer and operator, trajectory constraint, TGM training objective and sampling procedure are identical in Section 4 and Appendix E.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TF-Bind-8, synthetic bit sequences, UTR, AMP and GFP with identical task requirements and data coverage (Section 6; Appendix F).

E2.justification: The GFN, SAC, PPO and TGM-variant comparisons retain the same comparator membership within each corresponding experiment in Section 6 and Appendix B.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F retain identical splits, model configurations, training budgets, hyperparameter sweeps and evaluation procedures, including 100,000 generated training samples per biological-design run.

E4.justification: The analyses of q in Section 6.1, hyperparameter robustness in Section 6.3 and higher GFN reward exponents in Appendix B.1 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 2 reports averages and standard errors over 15 seeds in both versions. Seed information and uncertainty-reporting practices elsewhere are also unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported results match, including Table 2's GFP average mode reward of 2.95 ± 0.08 for TGM with q = 0.25. The plotted results and Appendix B's parameter-sweep and training-throughput results are identical.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, operator bounds, robustness results and trajectory-constraint proofs are identical across Sections 3–5 and Appendices A, C, D and E.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about GM interpolation, TGM's quality/diversity benefits and the robust-RL interpretation of regularization.

C2.justification: The interpretations of accumulation and dilution, compositional reward uncertainty, baseline credit-assignment difficulties and hyperparameter effects are unchanged. No limitations or applicability qualifications are added or removed.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, proxy-model training, data processing and compute disclosures in Appendix F are identical. The code-access link and runtime information in Appendix B.2 also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix A.5 and the bibliography are identical, preserving the same citations and positioning relative to GFlowNets, regularized RL and robust MDPs.

P1.justification: The first-page author line replaces 'Nikolay Malkin' with 'Esmeralda S. Whitammer'. The arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 9 Oct 2025 to v3 dated 31 Aug 2026. The remaining prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–4 retain identical graphics, captions, formatting and placement. Rendered pages 2–29 match pixel-for-pixel; the first-page text substitutions preserve its layout.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, empirical evidence, proofs, reproducibility information and presentation of results are identical, including the appendices. The author-name substitution and updated version/date stamp provide no evidence of a meaningful improvement or deterioration in overall paper quality.
